us-med-lab-professionals-limited-ai-ml-a.body: Posted in last 7 days U.S. Med Lab Professionals - Limited AI/ML Adoption in Molecular Dx Lab professionals: I could use your perspective on a finding that surprised me. I'm working on Medical Laboratory Observer's 2026 State of the Industry survey article on molecular diagnostics, and one result caught my attention: Among respondents who answered our question about AI/ML, nearly 70% said their labs aren't currently using AI/ML tools for molecular diagnostics — and have no plans to. With so much discussion about AI across healthcare, I'd like to better understand what's happening on the ground in the laboratory. If you're a U.S. medical laboratory professional, I'd love to hear from you: Why do you think adoption remains limited? Is it cost? Lack of a compelling use case? Workflow and integration challenges? Regulatory or validation concerns? Staffing and competing priorities? Or something else entirely? I'm looking for one or two lab professionals willing to share their perspective for the article. A brief conversation or email response is fine. Feel free to comment, message me or tag someone who might have insight. #MedicalLaboratory #LabProfessionals #MolecularDiagnostics #LaboratoryMedicine #ArtificialIntelligence #ClinicalLaboratory #MedLab Medical Laboratory Observer

engineering-teams-using-ai-agents-pr-rev.body: Posted in last 7 days Engineering Teams Using AI Agents - PR Review Capacity Strain AI made writing code cheap. It did not make engineering judgment cheap. As coding agents get better, I keep seeing the same bottleneck move downstream: More code → more pull requests → the same number of humans capable of reviewing them. I’ve experienced this firsthand while working on a cybersecurity product used in environments where reliability and security genuinely matter, including critical infrastructure. There was understandable pressure to turn the productivity gains from AI-assisted development into dramatically faster delivery. But that eventually leads to a much harder question: Who takes responsibility for code that no human has ever reviewed? Having one agent write the code and another approve it may make the throughput numbers look fantastic. It does not magically transfer accountability. I’ve since had similar conversations with people at other companies facing the same problem. The challenge is increasingly not “how do we get agents to write more code?” It is: How do we safely process all the code they already produce? In my latest article I explore what I think the next generation of the review pipeline needs: • deterministic automated verification • independent agent review • risk-based classification • human attention focused where judgment actually matters • smaller, reviewable changes • merge queues • WIP limits when the review queue is already full I also go into what I’m experimenting with in vincent and, more importantly, the parts I still haven’t solved. Coding faster is not the same thing as delivering faster. Code is getting cheap. Judgment isn’t. And trust may become the most expensive resource in the entire software lifecycle. 👉 https://lnkd.in/djJK9dnQ I’d especially like to hear from teams already dealing with this: are agent-generated PRs starting to overwhelm your review capacity? #SoftwareEngineering #AI #AgenticAI #CodingAgents #DevTools #EngineeringLeadership #SoftwareArchitecture

research-team-leads-ai-agents-reshaping-.body: Posted in last 7 days Research Team Leads - AI Agents Reshaping Research Workflows Agents might be the technology story of 2026. Everyone's watching engineering and design. But Anthropic's newly released “State of AI Agents Report” has a line we can't stop thinking about: among 500 technical leaders, research and reporting was the highest target for agent deployment for the next 12 months — ahead of supply chain, product development, and financial planning. Why is “research” a top priority for agentic workflows? The report thinks leaders are making a bet. Research spans every function and level of an organization, making it a “high-leverage starting point.” Research and reporting might also demonstrate ROI, including from AI initiatives. In our broader literature review, we haven’t found great explanations for when and why organizations are investing in agents for UX research. We think there’s a lot to learn about how agents are doing research inside teams day to day, and how research-as-a-function is changing as companies integrate agents and personas. Velocity Ave is partnering with Booking to explore how agents, skills, and AI-driven workflows are actually reshaping research. If you're leading a team and have thoughts about this early research puzzle, we'd like to hear from you. You can comment here, DM me, or write to us: [email redacted] Velocity Ave

babalawo-and-african-technologists-ifa-o.body: Posted in last 7 days Babalawo & African Technologists - Ifa Odu Meets AI & Neuroscience What should African youth do with the knowledge our ancestors left behind? This article uses the Yoruba Ifá system—and its 256 Odù—as a starting point for a broader conversation about tradition, science, AI, neuroscience, and cultural revival. My argument is simple: we should not choose between blindly accepting ancient claims and dismissing them as superstition. Respect the tradition. Study the knowledge. Don’t stop at magic—investigate. I’d especially like to hear from Babaláwo, scholars, scientists, technologists, and young Africans thinking seriously about where our inherited knowledge should go next. #Africa #Nigeria #Yoruba #Ifa #AI #Neuroscience #AfricanKnowledge #Innovation #Binaryology
